name: Wairarapa
scope: Existing destination wairarapa (11 spots, ids wairarapa-1..8, 10, 11, 12; wairarapa-9 appears nowhere in git history) plus the 5 Wellington-region standalone spots. Pipeline C step 1: sourced facts, ticketUrl verification, flags. No photos researched.

what_where.fact: The south-eastern corner of the North Island, separated from the Wellington metropolitan area by the Rimutaka/Remutaka Ranges, popular with Wellington day-trippers and commuters (over 1000 people commute 'through the hill' daily). Wikivoyage's towns: Carterton, Featherston, Martinborough, Masterton (the largest town), Pahiatua (Pahiatua is outside the Wellington Region; the Wairarapa is an 'unofficial region' per Wikipedia). Wikivoyage: the Rimutaka and Tararua ranges shelter it from prevailing westerlies, giving a warm, dry climate; wine is centred on Martinborough, with smaller areas at Gladstone and north of Masterton.

current_entry.tagline: Pinot noir country, pretty towns and a wild south coast.

span_check.verdict: All 11 spots are inside 67.5 km. Castlepoint (61.7) and Pukaha (58.8) are the closest to the limit. The 90 km span is justified by these two.

destination_facts.centre_note: The stored centre (-41.25, 175.65) is a rural point east of Martinborough near Lake Wairarapa/Pirinoa, not a town; Martinborough is at -41.2188, 175.4592 (Wikipedia/Nominatim). Acceptable as a regional centroid, but a pin there is not on a place visitors know. Unverified whether the pin renders sensibly; consider Masterton (-40.97, 175.65) or Martinborough. Left as is unless the owner decides.
destination_facts.rank_check: Rank 4 matches COVERAGE.md ('worth a detour if you are nearby'); Wairarapa is a Wellington day-trip region. No change suggested.

description_claims.claim: Just over the Remutaka Range from Wellington
Known for its wineries, especially around Martinborough
description_claims.status: supported (Wikivoyage: main growing area is around Martinborough, pinot noir and sauvignon blanc the two main varieties; Wikipedia: Martinborough has a large number of vineyards, notably pinot noir)

description_claims.claim: Towns such as Greytown and Masterton have historic main streets, cafes and boutiques
description_claims.status: UNSOURCED for Masterton: none of the loaded sources describes a historic main street there (Wikivoyage Masterton lists Aratoi, a sheep and shearing museum, a park). Greytown's Victorian main street is also not stated in the loaded Wikivoyage/Wikipedia extracts (Wikipedia Greytown covers history and the Arbor Day first celebration). Suggest rewording or sourcing from Destination Wairarapa (https://wairarapanz.com/, loaded, title 'Destination Wairarapa', but no main-street text read).

description_claims.claim: South coast has Cape Palliser's lighthouse, seal colonies and the Putangirua Pinnacles
description_claims.status: supported (Wikivoyage lists the lighthouse with the North Island's largest fur seal colony; DOC Putangirua page). 'seal colonies' plural is loose: Wikivoyage describes one large colony along the road to the lighthouse.

goodToKnow_checks.tip: Day-trip from Wellington: the Wairarapa Line runs trains to Masterton, and Martinborough is about 90 minutes by road
goodToKnow_checks.status: PARTLY SUPPORTED. Wairarapa Line: Masterton-Wellington, 91 km, five services each way Mon-Fri and two each way on weekends and public holidays (Wikipedia, Wikivoyage), so a weekend day trip by train is limited to one morning and one evening service; the stored tip does not say this. Martinborough has no train: Wikivoyage says Metlink bus 200 runs from Masterton and Featherston. '90 minutes by road' is not stated in any loaded source (Wikivoyage: Martinborough is 65 km east of Wellington). Also the tip omits Remutaka Hill Road: a narrow winding 15 km road, 'one of the country's worst crash blackspots' (Wikivoyage), and the Stonehenge site header warns to check Remutaka Hill closures. Suggest rewording around trains (weekend limit) and bus 200 and the hill road.

goodToKnow_checks.tip: Book a designated driver: wineries close together in Martinborough, cycling or a tour avoids drinking and driving
goodToKnow_checks.status: plausible; 'close together' consistent with Wikivoyage Martinborough Wine Centre offering cycle hire and Wikipedia saying vineyards sit in ribbons around the northern and eastern sides of town. No source explicitly says cellar doors are walkable/cyclable; Wikivoyage Wine Centre text was cut off at 'Cycle hire is'. Generic but acceptable.

goodToKnow_checks.tip: Keep your distance from seals: fur seals at Cape Palliser can be aggressive if approached, so stay at least 10 metres away
goodToKnow_checks.status: WRONG NUMBER. DOC advises staying at least 20 metres from seals (DOC media releases 2017 and 2021: 'Stay at least 20 metres away', 'keep your distance, at least 20 metres'), keep dogs on a leash and away, do not get between a seal and the sea. Change 10 to 20. 'Can be aggressive' is supported by DOC ('sharp teeth and can move quickly if they feel threatened').

best_months.blurb_stored: {months} are the best for wine tasting and for the south coast drive.
best_months.status: UNVERIFIED. Only a warm, dry climate (Wikivoyage) was found; no NIWA/Wikipedia climate table loaded and no source for a Nov-Apr recommendation. The Toast Martinborough wine festival is in November (Wikipedia Martinborough), which is an event, not a reason for month choice. Keep as is but flag.

cross_entry_repetition: Rimutaka Incline story appears in three places: standalone 'Rimutaka Incline' (bio: heritage rail formation), 'Fell Locomotive Museum' (bio: 'one of those that worked the Remutaka Incline') and Wairarapa/Remutaka FP. This is a genuine near-duplicate risk: DOC's page for the incline is the 'Remutaka Rail Trail' (18 km Kaitoke to Cross Creek); Wikipedia 'Rimutaka Incline' says the term is sometimes used incorrectly for the whole closed line and the incline formation is now part of the Rail Trail. Keep distinct by making the Incline bio about the trail and the museum bio about the locomotive.

Mount Holdsworth (Wairarapa-7) bio mentions 'the Southern Crossing' as a start point, and standalone Tararua Southern Crossing bio says it ends at Mount Holdsworth. Neither is right per DOC (see standalone section).

'The Lord of the Rings' appears in the Putangirua bio (Paths of the Dead) and the Kaitoke bio (Rivendell). Both true and in separate places; just avoid reusing phrasing in the destination description.
Tararua Forest Park and Remutaka Forest Park bios both open 'A ... forest park ...' with 'managed by'/'tracks' phrasing; the Kaitoke bio and Remutaka bios both say 'tracks'. Minor.

spots.name: Martinborough
bio_facts: Town of about 1,900 residents (Wikivoyage 2025), 35 km south-west of Masterton and 65 km east of Wellington; laid out by John Martin in 1879 with a Union Jack street plan

Large number of vineyards, notably pinot noir; almost all vineyards sit in thin ribbons around the northern and eastern sides of the town and on the Dry River to the south, following dry riverbeds, with a warm micro-climate

Wikipedia names notable wineries: Schubert, Te Kairanga, Tirohana Estate, Palliser Estate, Dry River, Martinborough Vineyard, Murdoch James, Ata Rangi, Craggy Range, Tiwaiwaka, Haythornthwaite, Escarpment
Toast Martinborough wine festival each November (event: description or best-time text only)

spots.name: Putangirua Pinnacles
spots.wiki_note: Wikipedia article title is 'Pūtangirua Pinnacles' (URL /wiki/Putangirua_Pinnacles redirects). Spot name has no macron and no wiki field; image lookup by name 'Putangirua Pinnacles' probably hits the redirect. Check the lookup resolves. Suggest wiki: 'Pūtangirua Pinnacles' only if the manifest key mismatches.
bio_facts: Earth-pillar (hoodoo) formations at the head of a valley in the Aorangi Ranges; Wikipedia: 'one of New Zealand's best examples of badlands erosion'; DOC: 'some of the best earth pillar formations in New Zealand'
Formed when Pūtangirua Stream exposed an ancient gravel layer; cemented silts or rocks that resist erosion leave individual pinnacles (DOC)
Eerie Dimholt Road / Paths of the Dead scenes in The Return of the King were filmed here (DOC, Wikivoyage)

Best view is from the lookout on Pinnacles Ridge Track; DOC recommends not approaching the base of the pinnacles; high rockfall and landslide risk including in the stream bed; stream can flash-flood so do not cross in or after heavy rain; no vehicles beyond the car park
Wikivoyage: the Pinnacles lookout is a 90-minute return walk from the carpark and DOC campsite; about 40 minutes' drive from Martinborough (DOC)
Car park, toilet, shelter and campsite near the reserve entrance (DOC)
spots.bio_suggestion: Eroded gravel spires reached by a walk up Pūtangirua Stream and a ridge-top lookout, used as the Paths of the Dead in The Lord of the Rings.
issues: Stored bio says 'reached by a river-bed walk'. DOC now says the best view is from the lookout on Pinnacles Ridge Track and advises against exploring the stream bed and approaching the base; 'river-bed walk' undersells the safety message. Suggest rewording to a walk up the valley/track.

Stored coordinates (-41.4468, 175.2468) are the pinnacles themselves (Wikipedia -41.4467, 175.2467) but the visitor standing point is the car park: DOC GPS -41.449483, 175.221505; Nominatim car park -41.45013, 175.22531. That is about 2 km west of the stored pin. COVERAGE.md says the pin should be the entrance/trailhead. Recommend moving to the car park (-41.4495, 175.2215, DOC).
spots.hours: Open 24 hours (open-access reserve; no hours stated by DOC; 'Open 24 hours' is a fair reading, daylight advised). Unverified.

visitHours.basis: Wikivoyage: lookout is a 90-minute return walk; 2-3 h consistent

cost.basis: No charge stated by DOC for the reserve; campsite fees are separate (not loaded).

spots.name: Cape Palliser Lighthouse
bio_facts: Built 1897; owned and operated by Maritime New Zealand; fully automated 1986
Reached by a staircase of 258 steps up a 58 m cliff, built in 1912 (Wikipedia; Wikivoyage also says 258). Stored bio says 250: WRONG
One of three NZ lighthouses with a striped paint scheme (the other two are black-and-white); this one is red and white (Wikipedia)

Cape Palliser is the southernmost point of the North Island; Wikivoyage: lookout across Cook Strait to the South Island, and the North Island's largest fur seal colony is on the coastal rocks along the road to the lighthouse
DOC: stay at least 20 m from seals, keep dogs leashed and away; do not get between a seal and the sea. Seals began breeding again at Cape Palliser in 1991 (Times-Age report summarised in search)
spots.bio_suggestion: A red-and-white striped lighthouse from 1897 at the southern tip of the North Island, reached by 258 steps, beside the North Island's largest fur seal colony.
issues: Stored 'reached by 250 steps' -> 258 (Wikipedia, Wikivoyage).
'near a fur seal colony' is supported by Wikivoyage; the bio should say the colony lies along the road to the lighthouse, not at the lighthouse.
spots.hours: Open 24 hours (open-access; no stated hours; Maritime NZ page not loaded). Unverified.

visitHours.basis: stored; climb of 258 steps plus seal viewing; plausible, unsourced

cost.basis: No entry fee stated anywhere loaded.

spots.name: Castlepoint
bio_facts: DOC: reef, lagoon, lighthouse and Castle Rock make 'a spectacular stretch of Wairarapa coastline'; about 1 hour from Masterton (turn into Te Ore Ore Road, becomes Masterton-Castlepoint Road); all walks begin at the road-end carpark
Castle Rock is 162 m high; the reserve is the only place in the world where the shrubby Castlepoint daisy (Brachyglottis compactus) grows, on the reef and Castle Rock
Fossil-rich limestone reef about 1 km long; seals, several dolphin species, white-fronted terns, red-billed gulls, black shags; reef herons and black-backed gulls nest on Castle Rock cliffs
Kupe named it Rangiwhakaoma ('the skies that race'); one of the earliest sites of human occupation in Aotearoa

Safety (DOC): beach is a shared area with vehicles and boats; high cliffs around the lighthouse and Castle Rock; DOC does NOT recommend climbing to the top of Castle Rock; the reef is extremely dangerous with rogue waves; no camping in the reserve (Castlepoint Motor Camp only); store and tearooms on the beach front
spots.bio_suggestion: A limestone reef, lagoon and 162 m Castle Rock on the Wairarapa's east coast, with a lighthouse walk and a rare shrubby daisy found nowhere else.
issues: Stored bio: 'a ridge walk over Castle Rock' CONTRADICTS DOC, which does not recommend climbing to the top of Castle Rock. Replace with the lighthouse walk (DOC: walks start at the road-end carpark; track times not loaded - UNVERIFIED).
Stored category 'viewpoint'; a beach/reef/lagoon scenic reserve might better be 'nature' or 'beach'. Judgement call; a lighthouse walk is the viewpoint.

Coordinates: stored (-40.9009, 176.2217) = Wikipedia settlement point (-40.8986, 176.2206) but the OSM lighthouse is at -40.9004, 176.2315, about 0.8 km east. Visitor standing point is the road-end carpark; exact carpark coordinate not found. Both stored and lighthouse are within a kilometre; low priority.

spots.name: Greytown
bio_facts: Rural town 77 km north-east of Wellington by road and 24 km south-west of Masterton on SH2
First settled 27 March 1854 under the Small Farms Association Settlement Scheme; named after Governor Sir George Grey
New Zealand's first Arbor Day celebration was held here on 3 July 1890; the town keeps a register of its trees (Wikipedia)
Train: Wairarapa Line stops at Woodside (for Greytown); bus link from Woodside to Greytown (Cobblestones site: Wellington Station to Woodside station then bus; not every train is met by a bus)

spots.name: Mount Holdsworth
bio_facts: Wikipedia: Mount Holdsworth is a rural locality in the Carterton District, about 17 km north of Carterton; the main eastern entrance to Tararua Forest Park

DOC: Holdsworth is the main eastern entrance to the forest park, 17 km from Masterton (rail and bus to Masterton); turn off SH2 onto Norfolk Road 2 km south of Masterton, then about 15 km to the Holdsworth road end
Holdsworth Lodge (DOC-bookable) sleeps 28; campsite near the road end; camping near the lodge is for lodge guests only; Donnelly Flat is a picnic area and campsite on Atiwhakatu Stream
Wikivoyage Masterton: Mt Holdsworth - Jumbo Circuit is a 24 km, 2-3 day tramp, 313 m to 1448 m, huts $5-15 per night (2017 listing)
Day-walk options from the road end (DOC): Atiwhakatu Track, Donnelly Flat Loop Walk, Holdsworth Lookout Track (near the lodge on OSM)
spots.bio_suggestion: The main eastern gateway to Tararua Forest Park, where a lodge, campsite and day walks lead to Mount Holdsworth and the Jumbo circuit.

spots.name: Fell Locomotive Museum
bio_facts: Railway museum in Featherston on the corner of State Highway 2 and Lyon Street, a short walk from Featherston station

Houses H199 'Mont Cenis', the only remaining Fell locomotive in the world (museum site and Wikipedia); one of six Fell locomotives that worked the Rimutaka Incline until 1955; Fell system used four horizontal wheels clamping a raised centre rail
Also a restored Fell brakevan, photos, video and memorabilia (Wikivoyage)
spots.bio_suggestion: A small Featherston museum holding H199 Mont Cenis, the last surviving Fell locomotive in the world, from the Rimutaka Incline railway.

Operator: 'a working Victorian heritage village'; village map for a self-guided walk; fully fenced site with gardens
spots.bio_suggestion: A heritage village in Greytown built around the old Hastwell stables, with a colonial cottage, a first hospital, a country school and a historic woolshed.

standalone.name: Rimutaka Incline
standalone.wiki: Rimutaka Incline (article title; name matches, no wiki field needed)
bio_facts: Wikipedia: a 4.8 km (3 mile) 3 ft 6 in gauge Fell-system railway at an average 1-in-15 grade between Summit and Cross Creek stations on the Wairarapa side of the old Wairarapa Line; the incline formation is now part of the Remutaka Rail Trail; the term is sometimes used incorrectly for the whole closed line

DOC: the Remutaka Rail Trail is an 18 km (Kaitoke to Cross Creek carpark) easy-to-intermediate walk, run or bike (4 h 30 walk, 1 h 30 bike from Kaitoke), part of the Remutaka Cycle Trail; Grade 2 bike; built 1878; Fell trains used from 1878 until the Remutaka tunnel opened in 1955

DOC: restored railway bridges and historic tunnels (take a torch), interpretation panels, viewing platform between Summit and Siberia tunnels with a view of the old Fell route up from Cross Creek, camping at Ladle Bend and Summit (Greater Wellington), flush toilets at the Summit
DOC: ranked one of the 10 most significant railway heritage sites in the world; the incline is known for extreme winds
Stored bio 'between Upper Hutt and Wairarapa' is acceptable: Kaitoke (Upper Hutt) to Cross Creek (Featherston)
standalone.bio_suggestion: The old Fell railway over the Remutaka Range, now an 18 km walking and cycling trail with restored bridges, tunnels and a viewing platform above the steepest grade.
issues: Name: DOC uses 'Remutaka Rail Trail'; the app's 'Rimutaka Incline' is the Wikipedia article and the historic name. The incline strictly is the 4.8 km Summit-Cross Creek section; the visitor attraction is the 18 km trail. Acceptable but consider the bio making this clear.
Overlap: this is a near-duplicate of the Remutaka Forest Park and Fell Locomotive Museum stories; also the Kaitoke start sits inside Kaitoke Regional Park. Treated as separate places; flagged.

Coordinates (-41.15277, 175.19545) are Wikipedia's incline point. DOC does not give a car park coordinate. Visitor access points: Kaitoke (-41.0496, 175.1791 area) and Cross Creek (OSM shelter -41.16719, 175.21608). Summit is ~2 km from the stored pin. UNVERIFIED which end a visitor 'stands'; stored pin is on the route so acceptable.
Stored hours 'Open 24 hours' fine for an open trail; DOC notes a section near Corner Creek was closed in 2022 (media release); current status UNVERIFIED.
standalone.hours: Open 24 hours (open trail; no hours stated). Unverified current closures.

visitHours.basis: DOC: 4 h 30 walk one way from Kaitoke, 1 h 30 bike; 2-5 h plausible for partial walks

cost.basis: No fee stated by DOC for the trail; camping fees (Greater Wellington) separate.

standalone.name: Kaitoke Regional Park
bio_facts: Wikipedia: regional park at Kaitoke, north-east of Upper Hutt; administered by Wellington (Greater Wellington) Regional Council alongside the Hutt Water Collection Area
Operator: location Waterworks Road, Kaitoke, Upper Hutt; 'super popular for picnics, camping, swimming and tramping, one of our most visited parks'

Walks: Weir Walk (15 min), Terrace Walk (30 min), Rivendell (15 min return; location of Rivendell in The Lord of the Rings with information panels), Loop Walk (swingbridge, 15 min), Pākuratahi River Walk (40 min), Swingbridge Track (1 h, Hutt River gorge views); longer walks include the Ridge Track
Camping first come first served at the Pākuratahi River campground (fees apply); swimming in the river; Kaitoke Weir collects almost half of Wellington's water

standalone.name: Tararua Forest Park
bio_facts: Wikipedia: 1,150 km2; established 1954 as the first of New Zealand's forest parks; highest peak is Mitre, 1571 m

DOC: outstanding variety of tramping, hunting and walking in a wild, natural landscape; main entrances are Holdsworth (east, 17 km from Masterton), Waiohine Gorge (southeast, via Dalefield Road south of Carterton, about 15 km gravel road with a ford) and Ōtaki Forks (west, around 19 km inland from Ōtaki, 1.5 h from Wellington)
DOC: frequently bad weather, open tops exposed to cold southerlies that have caused several fatalities, routes across the tops are for experienced trampers only
standalone.bio_suggestion: New Zealand's first forest park, 1,150 square kilometres of ridges, tramping tracks and huts in the Tararua Range, entered from Holdsworth, Waiohine Gorge or Ōtaki Forks.
issues: Stored bio 'a large forest park of ridges and tramping tracks above the Kāpiti and Wairarapa plains, managed by DOC' - supported in substance. Adding the first-forest-park fact makes it distinctive.
Stored visit hours 3-8 and 'Open 24 hours' are a trailhead-visit approximation; multi-day tramps outside that. Acceptable.

Coordinates (-40.83, 175.39) are Wikipedia's park point (Nominatim -40.789, 175.377); both are inside the range, not a visitor access point. For a park, acceptable per WRITING.md ('main visitor hub or visual centre'), but there is no such hub; Holdsworth (wairarapa-7) is the best-known entrance.
Overlap with Mount Holdsworth (wairarapa-7) and the Southern Crossing (standalone): keep this entry about the park; do not repeat the Holdsworth lodge detail.

cost.basis: No park fee; hut/campsite fees separate (not loaded).

standalone.name: Remutaka Forest Park
bio_facts: DOC: 22,000 ha park covering much of the Remutaka Range, easily accessible from Wellington, popular with trampers and hunters; Wikipedia: 220 km2, established 1972, six bookable huts, borders Pakuratahi Forest and the Tararua Range
Catchpool Valley (30 km from Wellington) is the most popular entrance, with a campground, tracks, picnic sites and swimming spots; it provides access to longer tramps in the Ōrongorongo Valley
Wairarapa-side entries along Western Lake Road: Cross Creek (start of the Rimutaka Rail Trail), Waiorongomai Track, Battery Stream/Papatahi Crossing, Ocean Beach
North Island brown kiwi have been released by the Remutaka Forest Park Trust since May 2006; some areas are closed to dogs to protect them
standalone.bio_suggestion: A 22,000-hectare forest park across the Remutaka Range with the Catchpool Valley campground, river swimming, longer tramps and kiwi released since 2006.

standalone.name: Tararua Southern Crossing
bio_facts: Wikipedia 'Southern Crossing': a tramping track in the Tararua Range, about 32 km, typically two to three days, beginning at Ōtaki Forks in the west, over Mount Hector, finishing at Kaitoke north of Upper Hutt

DOC: one of the four classic tramps of the Tararua Range; 3 days, 'Advanced tramping track'; originally the route from Ōtaki Forks to the Wairarapa Plains and later to the Kaitoke Basin; popularised in the 1920s-30s by the Tararua Tramping Club

DOC leg times: Ōtaki Forks - Field Hut 3-4 h (5 km); Field Hut - Kime Hut 3-4 h (5 km); Kime Hut - Alpha Hut 5-6 h (7.5 km) over Mount Hector (1,529 m); Alpha Hut - Kaitoke 8-9 h (17 km); alpine section Table Top to Mount Alpha (1361 m) about 6-8 h

Huts: Field Hut, Kime Hut and Alpha Hut, category Standard, 20 bunks each; tops notorious for strong winds, mist, freezing temperatures; DOC factsheet notes several fatalities on the Field Hut to Alpha Hut stretch

Access: Ōtaki Gorge Road, last 5 km unsealed; a search summary of a DOC page said Ōtaki Gorge Road was closed to vehicles after a slip and Ōtaki Forks campsite closed (undated) - CURRENT STATUS UNVERIFIED
standalone.bio_suggestion: A three-day, roughly 32 km alpine tramp from Ōtaki Forks over Mount Hector to Kaitoke, one of the four classic Tararua crossings and for experienced trampers only.
issues: Stored bio 'two-day tramp ... between Ōtaki Forks and Mount Holdsworth' is WRONG on both counts: the Southern Crossing ends at Kaitoke (DOC and Wikipedia), and DOC says 3 days (Wikipedia: two to three). The Ōtaki Forks to Holdsworth route is the separate 'Tararua Middle Crossing' (DOC: 4 days, expert route). Fix the bio.

Stored visitHoursMin/Max 16-24 (two days): change to ~24-48+ of walking, or a range reflecting 2-3 days; the field is hours a typical visitor spends; DOC's leg times sum to roughly 19-24 h of walking over 3 days.

Stored hours 'Open 24 hours; hut booking required' - UNVERIFIED that bookings are required: DOC lists the huts as 'Standard' category (typically ticket-based, no booking) and the loaded page text does not say booking is required. Hut fees not loaded. Remove 'booking required' unless sourced.
No cost stored; hut fees not confirmed (Wikivoyage Masterton lists $5-15 per night for Holdsworth-area huts in a 2017 listing, not these huts). UNVERIFIED.
